name: Object-Oriented Design
description: Modelling software with classes and objects using encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and common design principles.

questions.question: Which statement best describes encapsulation?
options: Creating many subclasses from one base class
Bundling data with the methods that operate on it and restricting direct access to internal state
questions.explanation: Encapsulation keeps an object's state and behaviour together and exposes a controlled interface instead of raw internals.

questions.question: In Python, what is the conventional name of the first parameter of an instance method?
questions.explanation: Python passes the instance explicitly as the first argument, conventionally named self; cls is used for class methods.

questions.question: Which statement describes polymorphism?
options: A class having more than one constructor
Hiding attributes with a leading underscore
Different classes providing their own implementation of the same method so callers can treat them uniformly
questions.explanation: Polymorphism lets code call shape.area() without knowing whether shape is a Circle or a Rectangle.

questions.question: What does the guideline 'favor composition over inheritance' recommend?
options: Build behaviour by holding references to other objects rather than extending deep class hierarchies
Put all code in one large class
questions.explanation: Composition assembles behaviour from collaborating objects, which is more flexible and less tightly coupled than inheritance chains.

questions.question: What does the Liskov Substitution Principle state?
options: A class should have only one reason to change
Depend on abstractions, not concrete classes
Objects of a subclass must be usable wherever the base class is expected without breaking correctness
Clients should not depend on methods they do not use
questions.explanation: LSP requires subtypes to honour the base type's contract; the other options describe SRP, DIP and ISP.

questions.question: Which design pattern lets you swap an algorithm at runtime by injecting an object that implements a common interface?
questions.explanation: Strategy encapsulates interchangeable algorithms behind one interface so the context can switch between them.

practical.title: Shape class hierarchy
practical.instructions: Write Python code for a base class Shape with an area() method, and two subclasses Rectangle (width, height) and Circle (radius) that each override area().
practical.expected_output: class Shape with area(); class Rectangle(Shape) and class Circle(Shape), each with __init__ storing attributes and an area() implementation (circle uses math.pi).

rubric.hint: Create a base class named Shape.

rubric.description: Uses pi for the circle area

tasks.title: Learn Python classes
tasks.description: Read the Classes chapter of the Python tutorial, covering instance attributes, methods, inheritance and private-name conventions. Recreate each example and modify it.
tasks.completion_criteria: You can explain self, __init__, inheritance and method overriding in your own words.

tasks.title: Model a bank account
tasks.description: Write a BankAccount class with deposit, withdraw and balance, rejecting invalid amounts. Add a SavingsAccount subclass that adds interest.
tasks.completion_criteria: Both classes work, invalid withdrawals raise an exception, and the subclass reuses the parent logic.

tasks.title: Apply SOLID and two design patterns
tasks.description: Refactor a procedural script (e.g. a report generator) into classes, applying single responsibility and dependency inversion. Implement Strategy and Observer from Refactoring.Guru in your own example.
tasks.completion_criteria: Refactored code with classes each having one responsibility, plus working Strategy and Observer examples.

tasks.title: Design a library management system
tasks.description: Design and implement a library system with books, members, loans and fines. Draw a simple class diagram first, use abstract base classes where appropriate, and keep persistence behind an interface.
tasks.completion_criteria: Class diagram plus working code where storage can be swapped (e.g. in-memory vs JSON) without changing business logic.
